body: Priority raised from P7 to P6: the owner of the AQ600L tests the LN2W post now and asks for taper. This issue waits for PR #4065 to merge (it changes the same post) and for the owner's answers on items 2 and 3 (corner motion under G51/G52, and the lean side). Questions sent to the owner on 2026-11-25.

Owner update (2026-11-25): he does not know how the LN2W control cuts a corner under `G51` / `G52`. He will look at it on the machine's graphics display tomorrow.

He does not use `G51` himself: it lets the control decide the corner rounding and similar details, so the output is not fully known from the program. He says it is the easier way, though.

This supports the refusal in the current post. Item 2 (corner motion) stays open until the owner reports what the graphics show. A second route to keep in mind: a program that states the top and bottom path explicitly (4-axis X Y U V), so CamCraft decides each corner and the verify step checks the same surface the machine cuts. Ask the owner which route he uses for tapers before choosing.

Owner input (2026-11-25), summarised in our own words:

**The owner cuts tapers as 4-axis programs, not with `G51` / `G52`.** He uses `G74` (4-axis on) with an explicit U/V position on each move, and `G75` (4-axis off) at the end. He avoids `G51` because the control then decides the corner shape.

**`TP` / `TN` in each mode:**

| Mode | `TP` (table to program) | `TN` (table to next) |
|---|---|---|
| `G51`/`G52`, die face up, size held at the top | part thickness (less the die land, if any) | 0 |
| `G51`/`G52`, die face down, size held at the bottom | 0 (or the die land) | part thickness |
| `G74` 4-axis | height of the part bottom above the table (usually 0) | height of the part top above the table (usually the thickness). **Required in 4-axis**: it sets the U/V plane. |

**Proposed route for this issue: 4-axis first.**
- CamCraft computes the bottom path (X Y) and the top path, and writes U V = top minus bottom on each move, between `G74` and `G75`.
- `TP` = part bottom above the table, and `TN` = part top above the table, from the setup (item 1).
- CamCraft then decides every corner, and verify checks the same surface that the machine cuts. That removes item 2 (corner motion) for this route.
- Lean side (item 3) becomes the sign of U/V, which a golden test can check against the top path.
- `G51`/`G52` stays refused until the owner confirms the corner motion on the machine graphics.

Waits for PR #4065 to merge (same post).
